unit.title: CSS: your first rule
unit.description: What CSS does, and how a rule is written: selector, braces, property, colon, value, semicolon

cards.definition: The basic building block of a stylesheet: a selector, then braces that hold one or more declarations.
cards.example: h1 { color: navy; } turns every main heading navy.

cards.definition: The name of the visual feature you want to change, written before the colon: color, font-size, background-color.
cards.example: In color: red; the part before the colon names what changes, here the text color.

cards.definition: What the feature is set to, written after the colon and closed by a semicolon: red, 18px, center.
cards.example: In font-size: 18px; the text size becomes 18px.

cards.definition: One property and its value written as a pair, like color: red; Several of them can sit inside the same braces.
cards.example: p { color: gray; font-size: 16px; } holds two of them.

cards.definition: Targets every HTML element with a given tag name: p styles all paragraphs, h1 all main headings.
cards.example: li { color: green; } colors every list item on the page.

cards.definition: A file, often called style.css, that holds all the CSS rules of a site, kept apart from the HTML.
cards.example: Change one line in it and every page that loads it updates at once.

choices: Styling a page: colors, sizes, spacing, layout
Writing the text and the headings of a page
Making the page react when you click
Storing the data of the site on a server
exercises.explain: HTML holds the content and its structure, CSS gives it its look, JavaScript gives it behavior.
whyWrong: Writing the content is the job of HTML.
Reacting to clicks is the job of JavaScript.
Data lives on the server side, in a database, not in CSS.

exercises.prompt: CSS can turn a heading blue without changing a single word of the HTML.
exercises.explain: CSS only describes how things look. The words stay in the HTML; the colors, sizes and spacing come from the CSS.

exercises.prompt: This rule makes every paragraph red. Which part is the selector?
exercises.explain: The selector comes first and says WHICH elements the rule targets. Here, p means every paragraph of the page.
whyWrong: color is the property: the feature that changes.
red is the value: what the property is set to.
The braces only wrap the declarations of the rule.

exercises.prompt: In this rule, what is color?
choices: The value: what you set it to
exercises.explain: Inside the braces, each line reads property: value; The property (color) names the feature, the value (blue) says how it looks.
whyWrong: The selector is h1, written before the opening brace.
The value is blue, written after the colon.
Comments are written between /* and */.

exercises.prompt: Which character separates a property from its value?
exercises.explain: A declaration is written property: value; with a colon in the middle and a semicolon at the end.
whyWrong: The semicolon closes the declaration, at the very end.
CSS never uses = between a property and its value.
Commas separate items of a list, such as several selectors.

exercises.explain: Each declaration ends with a semicolon. The closing brace ends the whole rule, after the last declaration.
whyWrong: The colon sits between the property and its value.
A period starts a class selector, like .price.
The brace closes the whole rule, not each declaration.

exercises.prompt: Build a rule that makes every paragraph (p) gray.
exercises.explain: selector { property: value; } Here p is the selector, color the property and gray the value.

choices: It colors the text of every h2 heading green
It colors only the first h2 heading green
It gives every h2 heading a green background
It colors all the text of the page green
exercises.explain: A type selector (h2) targets every element with that tag. color changes the color of the text.
whyWrong: A type selector targets ALL the elements with that tag, not just the first.
That would be background-color; color is the text color.
Only h2 elements are targeted, nothing else.

exercises.prompt: The heading stays black instead of turning red. Which line has the mistake?
exercises.explain: Between a property and its value you need a colon: color: red; With =, the browser does not understand the line and skips it.

exercises.prompt: Where is the CSS of a whole website usually written?
choices: In a separate .css file linked from each page
Inside the text of each paragraph
In the title of the page
exercises.explain: A stylesheet (for example style.css) holds the rules. Every page that links to it gets the same look.
whyWrong: The text is content: styles are not written inside it.
The title is only the text shown in the browser tab.
Image files hold pixels, not CSS rules.

exercises.prompt: Inside one pair of braces, you can write several declarations, one after another.
exercises.explain: p { color: gray; font-size: 18px; } sets both the color and the size of every paragraph.

exercises.prompt: Build a rule that makes every main heading (h1) navy.
exercises.explain: h1 { color: navy; } The selector h1 targets every main heading; color sets the color of its text.
